title: A New Year Challenge
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This New Year's piece diagnoses over-agreement — saying 'Yes' too often — as a habit that quietly drains people of the time and energy their real priorities need. The author runs through a litany of underlying motives for chronic yes-saying, from wanting to be liked to underestimating future costs, before proposing a simple discipline: track how long you can go without an unwise 'Yes.' The framing borrows the idea that a strong existing 'Yes' makes it easier to say 'No' elsewhere, turning the challenge into a test of priority clarity rather than willpower alone.
points: Chronic over-agreement is driven less by generosity than by a bundle of self-interested motives, from wanting to be liked to fear of missing out.
The real fix isn't forcing more 'No' answers — it's strengthening commitment to existing priorities so 'No' becomes the easier, natural choice.
The proposed New Year's discipline is to track how many consecutive days pass without saying 'Yes' to something you shouldn't have agreed to.
Even a modest reduction in unwise 'Yes' responses compounds into meaningfully greater productivity over a year.
quotes: You say 'Yes' far too often. You agree to attend, participate, speak, and lend a hand to others more often than you should.
Every time you say 'Yes' to requests and invitations you shouldn't, the priorities that form the basis for your effectiveness and success are deprived of much-needed energy and focus.
It is always easier to say 'No' when you have a strong 'Yes' somewhere else.
How many days can you count without saying 'Yes' to a request you shouldn't have?
Productivity depends on the discipline to say 'No' instead of 'Yes' more often. The clock starts today.
